static_findings: Full normalized source parts are bound by exact inventory membership, row counts, canonical hashes and caller caps. Origin bytes/listing exhaustion/schema normalization remain independently audited collector responsibilities.
Fixed-address selection scans all accepted log rows and ignores topics/amounts/labels; no core-emitter means no selected transaction even if an external transfer mentions the core.
Preparation recomputes and canonically compares the sealed selection, expands all logs only within selected transactions, and retains explicit status/order/core payload checks.

All declared transaction rows and block headers are required; exact positions/counts, header linkage, strict timestamp and adjacent UTC anchors are checked. This is intentionally stronger than a selected-status-only source interface.
Covered-empty selection accepted only when all declared source tables/parts and structural checks pass. Missing/partial source is not zero.
Sixteen copied owned source segments match frozen original AST source text byte-for-byte; no scoring or decoder semantics changed. Public runtime no longer depends on private collector.

resolved_review_issue.issue: Python object equality allowed Boolean/integer aliasing in sealed selection identity
resolved_review_issue.resolution: Canonical byte equality now rejects this alias, with new focused producer test. Earlier16/17test runs remain explicitly accounted;18 is distinct finalcount, not cumulativeexecutions.

integration_limit: Adapter emits day selections and archive observation objects; whole-window assembler/collector and real source audit still required. Source audit hashes are externally accepted attestations, not proof from syntax alone. Driver v1 and adapter explicitly support Ethereum chain1.
